title: Web Developer Roadmap
summary: Build strong web fundamentals first, then develop frontend and backend capability, followed by accessibility, performance, security, testing and deployment.

facts.Timeline assumption: Four-year B.Tech/B.E. programme beginning in 2026 and ending around 2030.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build and deploy accessible, responsive websites and web applications, with evidence in GitHub and a portfolio.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Develop depth in frontend, backend, full-stack, performance, accessibility or cloud.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Own larger web systems, architecture, performance, security and delivery.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine web expertise with emerging technologies, AI-assisted development, architecture and technical leadership.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Web development will continue to change at the tooling layer. Keep the fundamentals—HTML, CSS, JavaScript, HTTP, browsers, databases, security and accessibility—strong while adding new frameworks, AI development tools and deployment technologies as they become relevant.

items: Senior Web Developer / Senior Frontend Engineer
blocks.label: Career progression

blocks.text: Typical years vary by employer and individual progression.

At senior levels, web development becomes broader engineering work: architecture, performance, security, reliability, accessibility, cost and technical strategy. Maintain strong knowledge of browser and web fundamentals while adopting new frameworks, AI-assisted development methods and platform technologies when useful.
